title: Dispatch: 19.5.12 inventory repair after Sol S1-S6 (attempt 2)
description: Repair PR #643 per Sol review eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.5 (read its notes: S1-S6, each with invariant, scenario, sibling analysis, closure, evidence). Defect CLASS (not six examples): inventory statements (operation, requiredInputs, exclusions, residualDmInterpretation, entryPoint, runtimeOwner) that do not exactly describe the implementation, and in-force operations omitted from the inventory. Closure: (1) repair S1-S6 exactly as their closure conditions state, with no runtime behavior change; (2) then re-derive EVERY remaining entry (all tool and engine entries) against its implementation with the same rigor: for each, re-read the tool/engine function and every branch it selects (bound vs unbound paths, participant-type distinctions, refusals that actually exist vs claimed guards, terminal cascades, idempotency claims, real function signatures), and correct any statement that overclaims a guard, misstates a branch, or names the wrong callable inputs; (3) re-check for omitted in-force operations along the progression/advancement, creation, rest, and campaign-binding paths (S6 is the example: getLevelUpEligibility, awardXp, grantMilestone); add truthful entries with existing evidence pointers. Keep model-facing text unchanged except resolve-check-v2 (D5). Update engine-capability-ownership reasoning if scope wording changes. Report a per-entry change log in bd notes (entry, what changed, code location justifying it) plus the list of entries re-checked unchanged. verify:worktree before commit; commit on this branch; do not push.

NEW SUSPECTED DEFECTS (report only): (a) accept_ambiguity_precedent description says supply ALL matching interpretation ids but schema maxItems is 1 and the run code requires exactly one. (d) set_suffocation tool description says the drop happens at the start of the next turn but the tool applies it immediately. (e) resolve_concentration rolls the d20 before checking the owner is concentrating (nothing persisted, but RNG advances). (f) applyLevelUp does not itself check eligibility, relying on callers.
